record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Let p be k-avoidable. 1. If the number of p-free words on k letters of length n grows exponen- tially with n, then an integer N0 exists such that, for every n > N0, there are circular p-free words with length n on k letters. 2. If the number of p-free words on k letters of length n grows polynomi- ally with n, then the set of possible lengths for circular p-free words on k letters has density 0 in the set N\{ 0}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 2 and let A be an alphabet of size k. A pattern is a nonempty word p over a set of variables. A word w over A is said to encounter p if there is a non-erasing morphism h from the variable alphabet to A^+ such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w is p-free. The pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exist infinitely many p-free words over A. A circular word of length n over A is an equivalence class of words in A^n under cyclic rotation; equivalently, a circular word of length n is p-free if every factor (read cyclically) of every linear representative is p-free.

Let f(n) denote the number of p-free words of length n over A. Prove or disprove the following two statements for every k-avoidable pattern p:

(1) If f(n) grows exponentially in n (i.e., lim inf f(n)^{1/n} > 1), then there exists N₀ such that for every n > N₀ there is at least one circular p-free word of length n over A.

(2) If f(n) grows polynomially in n (i.e., f(n) = O(n^c) for some constant c), then the set
   S = { n ∈ ℕ \ {0} : there exists a circular p-free word of length n over A }
has density 0 in ℕ \ {0}, that is, |S ∩ {1,...,N}|/N → 0 as N → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate related results are known: for binary circular words there is a sharp threshold (circular binary words avoiding (7/3)+-powers exist for all sufficiently large lengths, while none of length large enough avoid k-powers below this threshold), and growth rates of pattern-avoiding languages are well-studied (overlap-free binary words grow polynomially, cube-free exponentially). However, no direct confirmation that the general two-part conjecture has been established in full generality was found; status is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial versus Exponential Growth in Repetition-Free Binary Words
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the dichotomy between polynomial and exponential growth for binary repetition-free languages with threshold 7/3.
status_evidence.claim: Supports the dichotomy framework underlying the conjecture but addresses only the binary repetition case.

status_evidence.title: Growth problems for avoidable words
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses growth rates of languages avoiding patterns and circular avoidance.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background context relevant to the conjecture without resolving it in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding or Limiting Regularities in Words
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on avoidability including circular variants.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys the area; full conjecture not reported as resolved.
